title: 11 Best UX Design Agencies in San Francisco
summary: Compare the 11 best UX design agencies in San Francisco, with verified locations, research versus design fit, accessibility deadlines and real cost ranges.
body_markdown:
**Key takeaways:**


- Ask any agency what SUS score its last project shipped at, because the System Usability Scale has a published research average of 68 across 500 studies and most firms never measure against it.
- Accessibility now carries a hard date: the Department of Justice requires WCAG 2.1 Level AA, with large public entities pushed to April 26, 2027 by an interim rule published in April 2026.
- Every location below was checked on the agency's own site, and three of the eleven are Bay Area rather than San Francisco proper, which we say plainly.
- UX research and UX design are separate purchases here, and two firms on this list sell only the first.


Hiring a UX agency in San Francisco is unusually hard for a reason nobody warns you about: the strongest firms are quiet. The teams doing serious research work for Salesforce or NASA are not the ones optimizing their way to the top of a "best UX agencies" listicle.


The lists that do rank well are also unreliable. One roundup we checked lists two different agencies with the same broken link. Another includes a compliance software company because it shares a name with a design studio. A third places a Los Angeles firm in San Francisco.


So we checked each agency's own site for what it does and where it sits. Eleven made it. We are first, and we have said clearly where a research-led specialist will serve you better than we will, including the point at which it makes more sense to[hire a UI designer](https://www.awesomic.com/hire/hire-a-ui-designer) outright.


## UX research and UX design are not the same purchase


The single most common mismatch in this category is buying research when you needed design, or the reverse.


UX research answers what people actually do and why: interviews, field studies, usability testing, synthesis. UX design turns findings into flows, wireframes and interfaces. Some firms do both well. Others are research houses that hand you insight and expect your team to act on it, and at least two on this list are firmly in that camp.


There is a third thing often bundled in, which is design systems and front-end implementation. That is closer to engineering than to either research or design, and agencies price it very differently.


Say which of the three you need in your first email. A research firm asked to ship screens will subcontract, and a production studio asked to run discovery will improvise. If you are unsure which applies, a scoped[UX audit](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ux-audit-report) is the cheapest way to find out before committing to a larger engagement.


## The 11 best UX design agencies in San Francisco


The table sorts on the distinction above, since research-led and design-led firms behave differently from the first meeting. Locations come from each agency's own site, with the real city named where it is not San Francisco.

The three peninsula firms are flagged in bold above. None of that is a mark against them, but it should not come as a surprise halfway through a kickoff call.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** product teams that need steady UI/UX work alongside everything else a release requires.


Our base is 156 2nd Street and our designers work remotely, with matching typically done inside a day. The work goes through a queue rather than a scoped statement of work, so app screens, the marketing site, the onboarding emails and the launch deck all come from people working to the same visual language.


That suits teams shipping continuously. It is a poor substitute for a dedicated research program, and we say so below.


**Core services:** product and interface design, design systems, no-code builds, identity, decks, motion and video. Copywriting and QA sit on All-in-One.


**How it works:**


1. Describe the flow or screen problem, with whatever research you already have.
2. A designer with product experience is assigned, usually the same day.
3. Iterate in Slack with unlimited revisions.
4. Pull the surrounding launch assets from the same subscription.


**Pricing:** All-in-One runs $2,995 monthly and Graphic Pack $1,490, each a fifth cheaper on quarterly terms. A Dedicated Talent option attaches one full-time creative plus a PM and is quoted per client.


**Where a specialist wins:** if your real problem is that nobody knows why users churn, hire EchoUser or Portigal first and bring the findings to us. We are execution capacity with design judgment, not a research house, and pretending otherwise would waste your money.


Want to talk it through?[Book demo](https://www.awesomic.com/demo) .


### 2. EchoUser


**Best for:** complex products where the design questions cannot be answered from the office.


Founded in 2006 in San Francisco, EchoUser takes a research-forward approach built on user journeys, personas and journey maps that feed into interactive design. Its client list is unusually heavyweight for a boutique, spanning Google, Cisco, Panasonic, Salesforce, NASA, Oracle and GE.


**Core services:** user research, journey mapping, interaction design, usability testing, UX workshops.


**Pricing:** no public rate card.


**Its real strength:** research depth applied to genuinely hard domains. If you already know the problem and just need screens drawn, the discovery phase will feel slow and expensive.


### 3. Portigal


**Best for:** organizations building a research capability rather than buying a research project.


Portigal is a San Francisco research consultancy whose stated aim is helping teams build a mature research practice, and its principal is one of the more widely read authors in the field. Note the framing carefully: this is research and research capability, not interface design.


**Core services:** user research, research operations and maturity, training and coaching, insight synthesis.


**Pricing:** not published.


**Where it fits:** teams that keep commissioning one-off studies and want to stop. Anyone needing shipped screens should pair it with a design team.


### 4. Impekable


**Best for:** teams that want design carried through into working software.


Impekable works from 2261 Market Street and describes itself as an award-winning product development consultancy, covering UI/UX design alongside mobile and web engineering. That combination removes the handoff gap where an approved design quietly degrades during build.


**Core services:** UX and UI design, mobile app development, web development, product strategy.


**Pricing:** nothing public.


**Why buyers shortlist it:** one accountable team from wireframe to release. If you have strong engineers already, you are paying for capacity you will not use.


### 5. Geekbears


**Best for:** startups moving from idea to a shipped first version.


Geekbears operates from 600 Chestnut Street and frames its offer as validate, design and build, which is the right order for an early product and a rarer sequence than it should be. The validation step is the one most startups skip and later pay for.


**Core services:** product validation, UX and UI design, web and mobile development, MVP delivery.


**Pricing:** unpublished.


**What it does best:** getting a first version into users' hands with the discovery step actually done. Enterprise teams with established process will find it lightweight.


### 6. RNO1


**Best for:** digital-first brands wanting experience design and brand identity from one team.


RNO1 is a San Francisco experience design agency working across brand and digital product for companies that live primarily online. The brand-and-UX combination matters when your interface is the main thing customers experience of your brand, which for most digital businesses it is.


**Core services:** experience design, brand strategy and identity, web and product design, digital growth.


**Pricing:** none published.


**Where it beats the alternatives:** coherence between how a product looks in market and how it feels in use. Teams with a settled brand needing pure product UX may find the brand layer redundant.


### 7. Frog


**Best for:** enterprises running experience design across markets and business units.


Frog runs a San Francisco studio as one node of an international network now owned by a large consultancy. For UX that ownership cuts both ways: you gain researchers and designers in many time zones, and you accept the governance layer that comes with a firm of that size.


**Core services:** user research at scale, experience and service design, design operations, strategy.


**Pricing:** enterprise-scoped.


**Why it earns a place here:** very few firms can staff a large, long design program to a consistent standard. Smaller teams will find the engagement model slow relative to a boutique.


### 8. Savas Labs


**Best for:** products where design decisions and engineering decisions are the same decisions.


Based at 40 Boardman Place, Savas Labs sells strategy, design, engineering and growth as one applied-intelligence practice. For UX specifically that matters when a product behaves probabilistically: interaction patterns the model cannot actually support get caught in the room rather than at handoff.


**Core services:** product and interaction design, engineering, applied AI, digital strategy, growth.


**Pricing:** not published.


**Its real strength:** the joined-up model, particularly for AI-inflected products. It is not a research house, so bring the user questions answered or budget for someone else to answer them.


### 9. Extractable


**Best for:** financial services and regulated organizations with complex digital experiences.


⚠ Extractable operates out of **San Mateo** in the 94402 zip. Several roundups file it under San Francisco anyway. Founded in 1999, it focuses squarely on user experience for enterprises, with a client list running to Visa, Charles Schwab, BMO Bank of Montreal and LendingTree.


**Core services:** enterprise UX strategy, research, experience design, digital transformation.


**Pricing:** not published.


**Why buyers shortlist it:** two and a half decades of regulated-industry work, which is exactly the context where generalist UX firms stumble on compliance and legacy constraints.


### 10. Clear Digital


**Best for:** B2B enterprises rebuilding a site or portal that has to serve several audiences.


⚠ The only street address Clear Digital publishes is **1570 The Alameda in San Jose** , though it does run a San Francisco location page alongside ones for New York and Chicago. It works as a B2B digital agency for enterprise clients, covering strategy, UX and build, with the multi-stakeholder complexity those sites always carry.


**Core services:** B2B digital strategy, UX and UI design, web development, brand.


**Pricing:** no published rates.


**Where it fits:** enterprise B2B work where the hard part is reconciling sales, product and marketing requirements into one navigable experience.


### 11. Eight25Media


**Best for:** enterprise teams needing web and UX delivery at volume.


⚠ Its own contact page gives **2055 Gateway Place in San Jose** , 95110, and lists no San Francisco office. A current UX roundup folds it into a San Francisco list without noting the distance. It is a B2B digital agency serving enterprises, with website design and delivery as the core practice.


**Core services:** B2B web design, UX design, development, digital marketing.


**Pricing:** not published.


**One caveat:** this is delivery capacity rather than a research-led consultancy, which suits a defined build and not an open-ended discovery question.


## How we checked this list


We started from the current San Francisco UX rankings and then verified every entry independently, which removed a surprising number of them.


A roundup published by one of the agencies in this category lists five firms, two of which link to a completely different company's website. Another well-ranked article recommends "Delve" as a San Francisco UX agency; the domain it points to belongs to a SOC 2 compliance software company, while the design firm of that name is a product innovation consultancy with no San Francisco address we could confirm. A third list includes SmallGiants, whose own contact page gives 925 N La Brea Avenue in Los Angeles.


We also dropped firms we would have liked to include. One long-established local studio lists no address at all, and we were not willing to assert a location on its behalf.


Three conditions decided the final list: the firm publishes where it is, UX is a practice rather than a service-page keyword, and the site loaded this month. Peninsula firms stayed in with their city printed next to their name, since twenty minutes of distance says nothing about the quality of the research.


## Two questions that separate real UX firms from the rest


Most agency evaluations turn on portfolio aesthetics, which tells you very little about whether a team can improve a product.


Ask what the last project measured. The System Usability Scale is the closest thing this field has to a standard instrument, and MeasuringU's analysis of 500 studies puts the[average SUS score at 68](https://measuringu.com/sus/) , with anything above that above average and below 51 in the bottom band. A firm that has never put a number on its work before and after is asking you to take design quality on faith.


Then ask about accessibility, because it is now a dated legal obligation rather than a nice-to-have. The Department of Justice's[rule on web accessibility](https://www.ada.gov/resources/2024-03-08-web-rule/) requires WCAG 2.1 Level AA for state and local government web content and mobile apps, and an interim final rule published on April 20, 2026 extended the compliance date for entities serving populations of 50,000 or more to April 26, 2027. If you sell to public agencies, universities or health systems, their deadline becomes your requirement.


Agencies that answer both questions crisply have done this work before. Agencies that redirect to visual craft are telling you something useful.


## What UX design costs in the Bay Area


Rates here are private almost without exception, so the practical approach is to price the model rather than the firm.


Model Typical cost What you get Best when


Subscription capacity $1,490 and up per month Continuous UI/UX plus surrounding design Product work is constant


Research-only engagement $20,000 to $75,000 Studies, synthesis, recommendations You do not know why users behave as they do


Product design project $50,000 to $200,000 Research, flows, UI, design system A defined redesign or new product


Design plus build $150,000 to $500,000 Design carried through to shipped software You lack engineering capacity


Enterprise program $300,000 and up Multi-team, multi-market design at scale Several products need aligning


Only the subscription row reflects a published price. The rest describe how firms at each tier characterize engagements, so confirm on a call rather than budgeting from this table. The genuine alternative to all of them is hiring, and the tradeoffs there are set out in our comparison of[UX specialists versus an agency](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ui-ux-specialists-freelancers-vs-ui-ux-design-agency) .


## Choosing the right one


Match the firm to the question you cannot currently answer.


Do not know why users drop off? EchoUser or Portigal, in that order depending on whether you want findings or a capability. Know the problem and need it designed and shipped? Impekable, Geekbears or Savas Labs. Brand and product need to feel like one thing? RNO1. Enterprise scale across markets? Frog. Regulated industry with legacy systems? Extractable. Enterprise B2B site or portal? Clear Digital or Eight25Media.


We fit when the UX work is ongoing and arrives alongside marketing pages, decks and launch assets, which describes most product teams between funding rounds. We are the wrong answer for a standalone research program, and the honest recommendation there is one of the two research firms above.


Before any of it, run the check that shortened this list: open the agency's contact page, confirm the city, and confirm the domain still belongs to the company you think it does. On this category that step is not paranoia, and it removed three otherwise credible names from a shortlist of[UX design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ux-design-agencies) we had already narrowed once.


## FAQs


### How much does a UX design agency in San Francisco charge?


Very few publish rates. Research-only engagements commonly run $20,000 to $75,000, product design projects $50,000 to $200,000, and design-plus-build engagements $150,000 to $500,000 depending on scope. Only subscription pricing is public here, starting at $1,490 monthly. Bay Area pricing carries Bay Area salaries, so expect quotes above what equivalent firms charge elsewhere.


### What is the difference between UX research and UX design?


Research establishes what users do and why, through interviews, field studies and usability testing. Design turns that into flows, wireframes and interfaces. Portigal and EchoUser lead with research; most others on this list lead with design. Buying the wrong one is the most common and most expensive mismatch in this category, so name which you need up front.


### Does my product need to meet accessibility standards?


If your customers include state or local government, public universities or public health systems, yes, and on a deadline. The Department of Justice requires WCAG 2.1 Level AA, with the compliance date for entities serving 50,000 or more people now April 26, 2027 following an interim final rule in April 2026. Even outside that scope, the same standards catch usability failures that affect everyone, which is why accessibility belongs in any serious[enterprise UX](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/enterprise-ux) program rather than in a remediation sprint afterwards.


### How do I judge whether a UX agency is actually good?


Ask for a measured outcome rather than a portfolio. The System Usability Scale averages 68 across 500 published studies, so a firm that can tell you where a product scored before and after its work is operating differently from one that shows you screens. Named clients with documented results, of the kind we publish as[case studies](https://www.awesomic.com/case-study) , are the next best evidence. Also ask who runs the research, since the person in the pitch is often not the person doing the interviews.


### Should I choose a San Francisco agency over one in the wider Bay Area?


Location matters less than discipline fit, and three firms on this list are in San Mateo or San Jose while doing work equal to anything in the city. What matters is whether they lead with research or design, whether they can build, and whether they have worked in your domain, which for mobile products often means checking their record among[app design agencies](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/app-design-agencies) specifically. Treat the address as a logistics detail, but do verify it, because plenty of directories get it wrong.
